At Just Eat, we persist a variety of data in the iOS app. In 2014 we decided to use MagicalRecord as a wrapper on top of Core Data but over time the numerous problems and fundamental thread-safety issues, arose. In 2017, MagicalRecord is not supported anymore and new solutions look more appealing. We decided to adopt Skopelos: a much younger and lightweight Core Data stack, with a simpler design, developed by Alberto De Bortoli, one of our engineers. The design of the persistence layer interface gets inspiration from Skopelos as well, and we invite the reader to take a look at its documentation.

Markdown-based memory with semantic search, hybrid retrieval, and offline-first sync between agents. Drop-in memory layer for any LLM workflow.

> **Multiple agents need shared memory?** SQLite-Memory syncs locally via CRDTs; pair it with **SQLite Cloud** (or your own Postgres/Supabase) to coordinate memory across machines, users, and workers. Free tier available.

Agent memory databases can be synchronized between agents using **offline-first technology** via sqlite-sync. Each agent works independently and syncs when connected, making it ideal for distributed AI systems, edge deployments, and collaborative agent architectures.

Modern AI agents need persistent, searchable memory to maintain context across conversations and tasks. Inspired by OpenClaw's memory architecture, sqlite-memory implements what we believe will become the de facto standard for AI agent memory systems: **markdown files as the source of truth**.

`sqlmem` is the Go CLI for managing SQLite Memory projects from the terminal. 1. **Cleanup**: Removes database entries for files that no longer exist on disk

2. **Scan**: Recursively processes all matching files - adding new ones, replacing modified ones, and skipping unchanged ones. Stored paths are relative to the scanned directory root, with local provenance retained only in local metadata.

Multiple agents can share and merge knowledge without any coordination. Each agent works independently with its own local SQLite database, syncing through a shared SQLiteCloud managed database when connectivity is available.

Each piece of text added to the database is parsed into chunks and tracked by a block-level LWW CRDT algorithm, which merges line-level changes from concurrent agents without conflicts. Only the portable `dbmem_content` table is synced — embeddings and local filesystem provenance are always local. After a sync merge changes `dbmem_content.value`, `memory_reindex()` recomputes stale content hashes and refreshes local embeddings.

An indexer that streams blockchain data from Envio HyperSync and stores it in ClickHouse for analysis. It contains no chain-specific logic: any network served by HyperSync can be indexed by naming its chain id, and every chain shares one database. One command, `indexer fleet`, runs all of them in one process behind a small password-protected web page.
Three blocks. Copy them in order. You need Docker with Compose v2.24+ and an Envio HyperSync API token (the free tier is enough to start).

That is the `fleet` service of `docker-compose.yml`: **one process, every chain**, with the control panel on **<http://127.0.0.1:8090/>** and one Prometheus endpoint on <http://127.0.0.1:9101/metrics>. Sign in with the password from step 1.

How Follow System works on Linux

On Linux, **Follow System** reads the XDG desktop settings portal's `org.freedesktop.appearance/color-scheme` preference and follows its live updates, including GNOME's dark-mode toggle with the standard Adwaita GTK theme. The resolved light/dark theme is applied explicitly to GTK window decorations and the webview. A portal value of `0` (no preference) resolves to light, so switching back to the desktop default cannot reuse the app's previously forced dark theme. If the portal is unavailable or returns an unsupported value, Tabularis falls back to the native window theme, then the browser media query. The default window capability grants `core:window:allow-set-theme` to allow native theme changes. macOS and Windows use native theme notifications. See the portal specification.

The data is an aggregation of publicly available sources: the official listing directories that exchanges publish (such as Nasdaq Trader, HKEX, NSE, the Japan Exchange Group, ASX, TSX, Deutsche Börse Xetra, Euronext and SIX Swiss Exchange), open reference data (OpenFIGI, SEC EDGAR, the ISO 4217 currency lists, CoinGecko) and contributions from the community. I strictly maintain the rule that all data in this database must be freely accessible to everyone. Data requiring paid subscriptions is never included. Information that companies charge for is typically owned and maintained by those companies, making public sharing of such data a violation of their Terms of Service (ToS). However, publicly available data can be freely shared (read more about the legality of web scraping here). This database will always remain <u>completely free</u>.

Upgrading does not need a new `init`. Agents run the server through `npx`, so they pick up a new release the next time they start. The design goal: a search that would come back empty relaxes instead (M8, in progress: L1–L5 exist as library code on search_relaxed; the default search path does not relax yet).
**Pre-alpha.** `PROGRESS.md` counts **390 of 588** MVP leaves done (66%), 0 in progress (last snapshot 2026-11-20). Post-MVP work is 0 of 180 and sits outside that percentage.
Format 1.0 is unstable until the v1.0 release (SPEC §15). The docs homepage plays this poster from `persia-hero.webm` and `persia-hero.mp4`.

`persia` does not export `Db` yet (M10). Under it, `persia-engine` creates and opens a database file, puts, deletes and commits documents through a WAL, merges segments, and runs a ranked search over a collection snapshot: user text compiled to a query, BM25F scoring, filters, sorts, facets, and pages. Relaxation (M8) is in progress as library code: `search_relaxed` runs the whole cascade: L4 `fuzzy` also reports "did you mean" corrections, and L5 `fallback` returns the collection's top documents by static rank or recency, flagged in the response (`"fallback"`). With the explicit opt-in `filters: "last_resort"`, one last step drops the request's filters when every level found too few hits, flagged as `"filters_dropped"`. Within a level, hits that need fewer edits rank first, and at L3 so do hits holding the other words as typed when L2 did not take them first (typo tiers). A request's `relax` options (`false`, or any collection key such as `min_results` or `fill`) merge over the collection's settings, and `explain` states the step each hit matched at. The `Db` facade is not built yet. The default search path (`CollectionViews::search`) does not relax, so a search that matches nothing returns no hits. A small CLI inspects and verifies files.

**Space:** dead frames (replaced segments, old manifests, consumed WAL chunks) are reclaimed by compacting the container (SPEC §4.6). The on-disk layout is a versioned format of this repository, specified in `SPEC.md` (draft v0.1). Anything written is little-endian and covered by a checksum. A layout change updates the SPEC, bumps a version or a feature flag, adds an ADR under `docs/adr/`, and adds a golden fixture. Segments are immutable once written.
|Container|`header.rs`, SPEC §4|Magic `PERSIA\0\x01`, format **1.0**, a 4096-byte header, two superblock slots, then frames. `format_major` 1 is the only major this build reads.|
|Segment|`segment/write.rs`, SPEC §5|Footer magic `PSEG`, format **1.0**. Sections, then the footer. `SegmentWriter` produces the bytes; `Segment::open` checks them.|
|CRC32C|`checksum.rs`|Castagnoli CRC on headers, frames, and blocks. A mismatch is `Error::Corrupt`, with the offset of the stored checksum.|
|zstd|`compress.rs`, ADR-0005|Block codec `Zstd` or `None`. Decode requires the uncompressed length the block header declared, and returns `Error::Corrupt` for any other length.|
|XXH3|`hash.rs`|XXH3-64 and XXH3-128, default secret, seed 0, for content and routing hashes. Integrity is CRC32C. Blob ids are SHA-256 (ADR-0002).|
|mmap|`mmap.rs`, ADR-0010|Read-only mapping of an immutable file range. A fault on a mapped page ends the process. Callers that cannot accept that use positioned reads.|
|`ByteSource`|`source.rs`|One buffer type for mapped, heap, and cached bytes. Clone and `slice` share the underlying `bytes::Bytes` (or the mapping) without copying the payload.|

|Unicode|`persia-analysis`, SPEC §6.3|UAX #29 word boundaries and NFKC, pinned to Unicode **17.0.0**. Built-in analyzers: `standard`, `keyword`, `whitespace`, `en`, `es`, `pt`, `fr`, `de`, `it`. Stemmers for German, English, Spanish, French, Italian, and Portuguese.|
|Fuzzing|`fuzz/fuzz_targets`, `.github/workflows/fuzz.yml`|cargo-fuzz on every target. Pull requests lint the fuzz crate. The scheduled workflow runs the targets on a dated nightly.|

|CI|`.github/workflows/ci.yml`|`rustfmt`, clippy `-D warnings` on the workspace and the fuzz crate, `cargo test --workspace` on Linux and macOS, format and storage tests on Windows, Miri on `persia-format` and the pure parsers of `persia-engine`, `cargo deny` (bans, licenses, sources), dependency direction, golden fixtures, and a fresh `PROGRESS.md`. Advisories run daily.|

`unsafe` is confined to modules an ADR names: the mmap reader (ADR-0010), mapped container reads (ADR-0017), and the OS calls `std` lacks (ADR-0021). Each `unsafe` block carries a `// SAFETY:` comment. Corrupt input is `Err`. The segment reader turns a bad segment into `ReadError`.
